## Upgrade note: consume defaults to read-committed

`kite consume`, with or without `-g`, now skips aborted transactions and
holds back records at or beyond the last stable offset while a transaction
is open. An idle-bounded read (`--idle`, or the 5 s default when stdout is
a pipe) can exit 0 with no records or only some of them, even with `-B`.
Use `--follow` to wait for the transaction to resolve, or
`--read-uncommitted` to restore the previous behavior: read to the high
watermark, including open and aborted transactional records. Use the same
isolation mode for all members of a group. (#99)

## Highlight: consumer groups

- `kite consume -g GROUP TOPIC` joins a Kafka 4.0 consumer-protocol group, shares partitions with other members, and resumes committed offsets. `-B` starts at the earliest offset only for partitions without a commit. (#97)
- kite commits offsets after flushing records to stdout, not after the downstream reader processes them. Without `-g`, consume does not commit offsets. (#97)
- `kite group list` and `kite group describe GROUP` inspect groups, committed offsets, and partition lag without changing offsets. Use `group list --all` to include classic groups. (#97)

## Highlight: transactional produce

`kite produce --txn ID TOPIC` writes all of stdin in one transaction. It commits on EOF and aborts on errors or interrupts before commit is sent. If interrupted after the commit request is sent, kite exits 130 and reports an unknown outcome instead of attempting to abort. This mode requires idempotence and broker-side transaction partition verification, enabled by default in Apache Kafka 3.6+. (#100)

## Also
- Group tables now align columns on terminals. Piped output remains headerless TSV, and JSON output is unchanged. (#98)
- Improved multi-broker and leader-change recovery. Standalone consume retries the refreshed leader before treating the gap in records as idle. (`12c323a`, `b5a2d09`)
